SIKAFLOOR®-08 PRIMER: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-08 Primer, April 2023, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sikafloor-08-primer.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-08 Primer where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sikafloor®-08 Primer is a versatile & economical priming concentrate.
    - When diluted 1:2 or 1:3 with water = 15L or 20L of mixed priming liquid. This consistency is used for priming porous concrete surfaces.
    - Alternatively Sikafloor®-08 Primer can be applied neat on suitably prepared timber/wood or cement sheeting substrates prior to Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Applied in combination with self-levelling compounds from Sikafloor® or Lanko® ranges. Sikafloor®-08 Primer:
    - Can be applied on interior or exterior concrete
    - Can be used in residential, commercial and industrial
    surfaces.
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - applications.
    - Can be applied on floors and walls where required
1.5 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-08 Primer
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: CONCENTRATED ACRYLIC PRIMER FOR FLOORING & TILING SYSTEMS
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates. Green Star VOC-SCQMD Rule 1168
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Fast drying
    - Solvent free
    - Can be applied over various substrates - concrete, timber/wood, cement sheeting
    - Great penetration into porous construction materials
    - Non-combustible
    - Suitable for internal or external applications
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Acrylic liquid
2.5 System structure. When Sikafloor® or Lanko® self-levelling products are applied
    | Porous concrete | Timber/wood/cement sheeting |
    | Sikafloor®-08 Primer (diluted) | Sikafloor®-08 Primer (neat) |
    | Sikafloor® or Lanko® self-levelling | Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel |
    | materials |
    | Chosen flooring | Chosen flooring |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.6 Mixing ratio.
    | Surface | Dilution & application |
    | Normal steel trowel concrete | 1:3 |
    | CSP 1 - CSP 2 | x 1 coat (broom or roller applied) |
    | Mechanically prepared concrete | 1:3 |
    | CSP 3 - CSP 10 | x 2 coats (broom applied) |
    | Cement levelling compound | 1:3 |
    | x 1 coat (broom applied) |
    | Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel | No dilution, apply neat |
    | x 1 coat (roller applied) |
    | Timber/wood/cement sheeting/wall | No dilution, apply neat |
    | lining | x 1 coat (roller applied) |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
    Note: Mix ratio & application device recommendations should be followed depending on the type of surface mentioned above.
    Not following these recommendations may result in poor performance and possible product/system failure.
2.7 Consumption.
    - 1:3 dilution ~ 6-9 m2 per mixed L
    - Neat ~ 5-6 m2 per L
    Average consumption is dependent on absorbency of the substrate, applicator device and mixing ratio.
2.8 Substrate temperature. Between+5 °C to 35 °C
2.9 Substrates. ▪ Internal or external porous concrete; ▪ Internal cement levelling compound; ▪ Internal Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel levelling compound; ▪ Internal timber/wood/cement sheeting/wall lining
2.10 Waiting time to overcoating. Before applying Sikafloor® or Lanko® products.
    | Substrate | Waiting time |
    | Porous concrete | ~10 - 20 min @ 23 °C |
    | Per coat |
    | Cement levelling compound | ~10 - 20 min @ 23 °C |
    | Per coat |
    | Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel | ~120 min @ 23 °C |
    | Per coat |
    | Timber/wood/cement sheeting/wall | ~120 min @ 23 °C |
    | lining | Per coat |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
    Note: All values are approximate and subject to climatic conditions.
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 5L plastic bottle
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production (in closed packaging)
    - Storage conditions: Store in a cool, dry place. Do not store below +5 °C. Material that has been mixed with water should be used within a week.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - ▪ All substrates should be fully cured, structurally sound ,clean, dry, and free of surface contaminates. Concrete substrate must fully cured at least 28 days old with a pull off strength of 1.5 MPa.
    - ▪ Cement-based substrates must be porous and accept water penetration. Test porosity by lightly sprinkling water on various areas of the substrate. If water penetrates, then a good bond with Sikafloor®-08 Primer can be achieved. If water beads and fails to be absorbed, surface contaminants are most likely present and a loss of adhesion may occur.
    - ▪ Surface contaminants that are present should be mechanically removed before installation of Sikafloor®-08 Primer.
    - ▪ All substrates must be free of efflorescence and not subject to hydrostatic pressure. If the cement-based substrate has efflorescence or high moisture (RH), Sikafloor®-158 W Fast Barrier + moisture barrier system should be considered.
    - ▪ Timber/wood/cement sheeting/Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel must be free of any previous coatings. The manufacturers installation guidelines must be followed when timber/wood/cement sheeting are first installed. Movement of sub-floors must be minimized by mechanical or chemical procedures prior to the installation of Sikafloor® products.
    - ▪ Please refer also to the product data sheets of subsequent suitable materials for further details.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Equipment.
    - Suitable mixing buckets, clean cool water, mixing drill & paddle.
    - Soft bristle broom or 12+mm napped paint roller.
4.3 ▪ apply diluted.
    - Sikafloor®-08 Primer by way of a soft bristle broom, or 12+mm napped roller. Correct amount of mixed primer liquid should always be applied to the prepared substrate, giving good penetration and film build. Thin applications may result in pinholing in the finished surface or debonding levelling compound from the substrate.
    - On particularly porous surfaces where the initial prime coat is absorbed immediately, or mechanically prepared surfaces a second coat is recommended. Avoid foam during application by adding more liquid.
4.4 ▪ apply neat. Sikafloor®-08 Primer over raw timber/chipboard, cement sheeting or Sikafloor®-4020 FiberLevel with a long napped roller 12mm+.
4.5 ▪ apply neat - Note.
    - For best practice it is recommended subsequent construction materials are applied as soon as primer is dry, but no later than 24hrs.
    - ▪ Care must be taken not to allow dust to settle on the freshly primed surface.
    - ▪ If dust has contaminated the surface, first vacuum clean and apply another coat of primer before subsequent materials are installed.
    - ▪ Do not allow primer to pool while drying as this will cause a soft spot under construction material.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.6):
    - temperatures below 5°C and above 35°C.
5.3 Basis of the stated values.
    - Manufactured in Australia.
    - All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-08 Primer, April 2023, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sikafloor-08-primer.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor 08 Primer, version 12/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/MSDS%20Sikafloor%2008%20Primer.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
